svg.title: Optional scoped study index for the XR cache-capacity comparison
svg.desc: A compact optional index into the XR cache study record. It shows the claim under review and twelve fields, from intent and task through direct enumeration, failed runs, rejection checks and authority, what the evidence supports, and the accountable decision. The comparison uses a rerun 2 MiB L2 baseline and 3 MiB and 4 MiB candidates under the same declared workload and tool conditions.
svg.text: At least one larger L2 reduces 99th-percentile frame time by removing
capacity misses while meeting the declared power, area, and timing checks.

g.text: Intent
Reduce XR tail latency without weakening
power, area, timing, or functional checks.
Task
Decide whether the 3 MiB or 4 MiB L2 should
advance beyond the rerun 2 MiB baseline.
Design space
2 MiB, 3 MiB, and 4 MiB L2 capacities;
all other architecture choices remain fixed.
Recorded study state
XR trace, frame IDs, cache configuration,
software image, power model, and tool versions.
Environment
Cycle-level simulator and SRAM model under
the declared workload and process conditions.
Method role
Directly enumerate all three legal capacities;
no learned method is required.
Feedback budget
Four cycle-level executions, including reruns,
plus one SRAM evaluation per capacity.
Evidence
Checks, misses, power, area, access time, and
uncertainty in the 99th-percentile frame-time change.
Failed runs / rejected alternatives
Links distinguish infrastructure failures from
candidates rejected by a declared check.
Rejection checks and authority
Functional, power, area, timing, and tail-latency
checks may reject; the architect owns waivers.
What the evidence supports
Open until valid returns pass checks and the
capacity-miss mechanism explains tail latency.
Accountable decision
The named architect may advance at most one capacity
to RTL evaluation; no signoff or product commitment.

svg.text: This optional card indexes the study record. It does not replace existing engineering records.
